newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Treasury stands by budget forecasts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Treasury stands by budget forecasts.

text.p: The Australian Treasury on Friday issued a quarterly report restating confidence in its three-month old forecasts, which support an overall outlook for 3.5 percent year-average gross domestic product (GDP) growth for the fiscal year to June 1997.
The Treasury's Economic Round-Up publication also described moderate price pressures in the economy.
"There have been some recent signs of moderation in aggregate wage outcomes," the Treasury said.

"Underlying inflation of 0.5 percent in the September quarter 1996 brought the year-to rate to 2.4 percent, down from 3.1 percent in the previous quarter and confirming expectations of low underlying inflation in the near term," Treasury said.
"Business surveys suggest a continuation of modest inflationary pressures at the same rate as recorded in the September quarter."
Some private economists think some of the forecasts that the Treasury issued with the August 20 budget were optimistic, particularly those for employment and investment growth.
But the Treasury, reviewing the latest data, said it found evidence supporting or consistent with its forecasts for:
-- Private consumption growth, forecast in the August budget at 2.75 percent year-average for the fiscal year to June 1997.
-- Dwelling investment, which it expected to trough and then recover in 1996/97.
-- Business investment growth, forecast in August at 14 percent, although Treasury now saw uncertainty in the timing of equipment investment.
-- Workforce growth, forecast in the budget at 1.5 percent.
-- The current account deficit, which is forecast at A$20 billion in 1996/97.
